newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram sees consumer demand rise -PTI.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram sees consumer demand rise -PTI.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said consumer demand would pick up and urged firms to take advantage of the stable rupee to import capital goods and technology, the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported.
"This is the time for us to take courage and invest in production and services. Consumer demand will pick up in four months from now," PTI quoted Chidambaram as saying in Madras on Saturday.

The finance minister said interest rates had come down by four percentage points since the centre-left United Front coalition government took office one year ago, and liquidity had ceased to be a problem.

The Industry Ministry said on Sunday that the year-on-year inflation rate as measured by the wholesale price index fell to 5.93 percent in the week ended May 31 from 6.00 percent in the previous week.

The news agency said Chidambaram told a reception in honour of a local industrialist that people must not "fall prey to the psychology of fear and suspicion", and the country was poised to achieve rapid economic growth.
The finance minister said credit conditions had eased after the Reserve Bank of India changed statutory reserve requirements.
Inflation had fallen, foreign exchange reserves stood at a record $24.7 billion and foreign direct investment was flowing into India at the rate of $300 million a week, he was quoted as saying.
Chidambaram said the exchange rate of the rupee was "unusually stable" and the currency's value would have strengthened if the central bank had not intervened.
The rupee closed unchanged on Friday at 35.83/84 against the U.S. dollar.
"This is the time to import capital goods and technology," PTI quoted him as saying. "This is the time to take advantage of the exchange rate to kick-start industrial activity in the country.
"Hopefully with nobody to rock the central government boat, the economy should see all-round growth, and I also hope industry will do much better this year," he was quoted as saying.
